en: Vāsudeva, Hṛṣīkeśa, Vāmana, Jalaśāyin,
Janārdana, Hari, Kṛṣṇa, the one whose chest bears the Śrīvatsa mark, and the one whose banner is Garuḍa.
To Vārāha, the lotus-eyed one; to Nṛsiṃha, the ender of Naraka;
to Viṣṇu, the unmanifest, eternal, infinite, unborn, and immutable.
Nārāyaṇa, the wielder of the mace, Govinda, the vessel of glory,
the god who lifted Govardhana, the sustainer of the earth, and the Lord of the universe.
The knower, the Person of Sacrifice, the Lord of Sacrifice, the Conductor of Sacrifice;
the Discus-wielder, the Mace-wielder, the Conch-wielder, the Supreme among Men.
Vaikuṇṭha, the subduer of the wicked, Bhūgarbha, the one clad in yellow garments,
Trivikrama, the knower of the three periods of time, Trimūrti, and Nandikeśvara.
Rāma, Rāma, Hayagrīva, Bhīma, Raudra, Bhavodbhava,
Śrīpati, Śrīdhara, Śrīśa, Maṅgala, and Maṅgalāyudha.
Dāmodara, endowed with self-restraint; Keśava, the slayer of Keśin;
the most excellent one, the giver of boons; Viṣṇu, bliss itself, born of Vasudeva.
The golden-seeded, radiant, ancient, and supreme person;
the whole and the partless, the pure, devoid of qualities yet the eternal abode of all qualities.
Resembling a golden body, with a radiance equal to ten thousand suns,
dark as a rain cloud, four-armed, skillful, and lotus-eyed.
He is the form of light and yet formless; his own nature is established in all forms.
He is the omniscient one, abiding in all forms, the Lord of all, whose face is turned in every direction.
Knowledge that is immovable and unshakable, the supreme Lord who bestows knowledge,
the Master of Yoga, proficient in yoga, the Yogin, whose very form is yoga.
I bow to the Lord of all beings, the Sovereign composed of all elements.
This divine hundred names of Viṣṇu is indeed the destroyer of sins.
Formerly narrated by Vyāsa, this [work] destroys all sins;
the man who recites it upon rising in the morning shall indeed become a Vaiṣṇava.
With his soul purified of all sins, he shall attain union with Viṣṇu;
[this is equal to] thousands of Cāndrāyaṇa penances and hundreds of gifts of maidens.
A man shall become a partaker of liberation through hundreds of thousands of cows;
that human being obtains the merit and fruit of ten thousand horse-sacrifices.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, Vāsudeva.
